# 4 Ezra Chapter 14 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Latin Vulgate (Codex Sangermanensis) | **Section:** Core apocalypse — Ezra restores the scriptures

---

**1** And it came to pass on the third day, while I was sitting under an oak, behold! a voice came out of a bush over against me, and said: Ezra, Ezra!

**2** And I said: Here am I, Lord; and I rose to my feet.

**3** Then said he to me: In the bush I manifested myself to Moses and spoke to him when my people were in bondage in Egypt;

**4** and I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to Mount Sinai, where I held him with me many days.

**5** And I told him many wondrous things and showed him the secrets of the times and the end of the seasons; and I commanded him, saying:

**6** These words you shall publish openly, and these you shall hide.

**7** And now I say the same to you:

**8** Lay up in your heart the signs that I have shown you, the dreams that you have seen, and the interpretations which you have heard;

**9** for you shall be taken up from among men, and from henceforth you shall remain with my son and with those who are like you, until the times are ended.

**10** For the world has lost its youth, and the times begin to grow old.

**11** For the age is divided into twelve parts, and nine of its parts have already passed,

**12** and half of the tenth part; and there remain two parts after the middle of the tenth part.

**13** Therefore set your house in order, and reprove your people, and comfort the lowly among them, and let go already of corruptible things,

**14** and renounce mortal considerations, and cast away from you the burdens of man, and divest yourself now of your weak nature,

**15** and lay aside your inmost thoughts, and hasten to escape from these times.

**16** For worse evils than those which you have seen shall be done hereafter.

**17** For look at the weakness of those who grow old: as they become older they become ever more removed from the truth.

**18** For you think that you shall grow in wisdom as you grow old; but the more you age, the more you shall fail in knowledge and understanding.

**19** For the world has entered on its decline.

**20** Then I answered and said: Let me speak before you, O LORD.

**21** For behold, I will go as you have commanded me, and I will reprove those of the present time; but who shall counsel those who shall be born hereafter?

**22** For the world is set in darkness, and they who dwell in it are without light.

**23** For your law was burned, and so no one knows the things that have been done by you, or the works that shall be done.

**24** If therefore I have found grace before you, send into me the Holy Spirit, and I will write everything that has happened in the world since the beginning — the things that were written in your law — that men may be able to find the path, and that those who wish to live in the last days may live.

**25** And he answered me and said: Go and gather the people together, and tell them to seek you not for forty days.

**26** But prepare for yourself many writing tablets of boxwood, and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Ethan, and Asiel — these five who are ready to write swiftly.

**27** And come here, and I will light in your heart the lamp of understanding, which shall not be put out until the things are ended which you shall write.

**28** And when you have done this, some things you shall publish openly, and some you shall deliver secretly to the wise; tomorrow at this hour you shall begin to write.

**29** Then I went as he commanded me, and gathered all the people together, and said:

**30** Hear these words, O Israel.

**31** Our fathers were strangers in Egypt in the beginning, and they were liberated from there,

**32** and received the law of life, which they kept not — which you also after them have transgressed.

**33** Then the land was given to you for an inheritance in the land of Zion; but you and your fathers committed iniquity and kept not the ways which the Most High commanded you.

**34** And forasmuch as he is a righteous judge, he took from you in time what he had given you.

**35** And now you are here, and your brethren are farther from you.

**36** If therefore you will rule over your own understanding, and instruct your hearts, you shall be kept alive, and after death you shall obtain mercy.

**37** For after death shall come the judgment, when we shall live again; and then shall the names of the righteous be manifest, and the deeds of the ungodly shall be declared.

**38** Let no one therefore come to me now, nor seek me for forty days.

**39** So I took the five men as he commanded me, and we went into the field and remained there.

**40** And it came to pass the next day that, behold! a voice called me, saying: Ezra, open your mouth and drink what I give you to drink.

**41** Then I opened my mouth, and behold! there was reached to me a full cup, which was full as it were of water, but its color was like fire.

**42** And I took it and drank; and when I had drunk of it, my heart poured forth understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit retained its memory;

**43** and my mouth was opened and was no more shut.

**44** The Most High also gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote in turn what was dictated, in characters which they knew not.

**45** And they sat forty days, and they wrote in the daytime, and at night they ate bread.

**46** But as for me, I spoke in the daytime and by night held not my tongue.

**47** So in the forty days there were written ninety-four books.

**48** And it came to pass, when the forty days were fulfilled, that the Most High spoke, saying: The first that you have written publish openly, that the worthy and unworthy may read it;

**49** but keep the seventy last, that you may deliver them only to such as are wise among your people:

**50** for in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the stream of knowledge.
